qa_pairs.question: Can users disable multifactor authentication for their accounts?
qa_pairs.answer: No, multifactor authentication is mandatory and users cannot disable it. Exceptions are only granted for automation purposes.

qa_pairs.question: What steps should a user take if they lose their second factor device for multifactor authentication?
qa_pairs.answer: If you have bypass codes or another registered device, use one of those to connect to your account on the portal, register a new device, and then delete the lost device. If you've lost all registered devices and lack bypass codes, you must email support@tech.alliancecan.ca with detailed account information, including your primary email address, research area, IP address, principal investigator, group members, frequently used clusters, software modules, and recent job IDs or support ticket topics/IDs.

qa_pairs.question: Which SSH clients are compatible with multifactor authentication?
qa_pairs.answer: Most command-line interface clients on Linux and macOS are compatible. Specific clients that also work include Cyberduck, FileZilla, JuiceSSH on Android, MobaXTerm, PuTTY, PyCharm, Termius on iOS, VSCode, and WinSCP.
